displayname.description: Has Significant Care or Medical Costs

REBOUND IN REVISION 0.8 from rev_likertresponse to rev_agreementresponse - see rev_wellbeinganswer8 for the evidence. This is the question closest to what the grant is for, and it is the one where the old frequency labelling read worst: an applicant who STRONGLY DISAGREED that they had managed a break would have been recorded as having had one 'None of the time'. The ordinal values and therefore the score are unchanged.

displayname.description: Overall, how satisfied are you with your life nowadays?

Description.description: Raw export column 95, the ONS life-satisfaction question: "Overall, how satisfied are you with your life nowadays?" A WHOLE NUMBER FROM 0 TO 10 - the raw answer the applicant gave, on the scale the question is published with. Asked FIRST on the live form, before the ten wellbeing questions. CONVERTED FROM A FIVE-OPTION PICKLIST IN REVISION 0.3, on the reviewer's confirmation that the score is out of 60 (10 + 10 x 5). This is the eleventh scored answer and the only one that is INVERTED before it contributes (FR-012): the contribution is 10 minus the raw answer, so 0 (worst self-reported wellbeing) contributes 10 points of need and 10 (best) contributes 0. The inversion is the FeelingScaleInversion row in the Setting table, keyed 0 to 10, never arithmetic inside a flow. WHY A WHOLE NUMBER RATHER THAN AN ELEVEN-VALUE OPTION SET: on a 0-to-10 scale the number IS the answer, so an option set would carry eleven labels that only repeat their own values, and option value 0 is not a safe picklist value in Dataverse (it is widely treated as 'no value', which would make 'worst possible wellbeing' indistinguishable from 'unanswered' - and this is the one answer whose absence must withhold the automated outcome under FR-022). MinValue and MaxValue bound the range in the schema, which is exactly how rev_circumstancescore expresses its own numeric range in this table. NULL still means unanswered; 0 is a real answer.
The date and time the scoring process last calculated this application's score.
Shows whether the process owner has manually changed the automatically calculated status.

The date this application was auto-rejected or rejected, which starts the countdown for how long the record is kept.

Whether a safeguarding concern has been raised against this application, independent of its processing status. SECURED: Admin + Service only, never trustee-visible - a staff escalation matter, not a funding-decision input.
Staff notes on the safeguarding concern, collected only when rev_safeguardingflag is true. SECURED: same basis as the flag itself - highly sensitive third-party welfare detail, Admin + Service only.
The applicant's free-text account of their circumstances, exactly as submitted.
The applicant's free-text description of a condition that is not covered by the standard list.
The general categories of condition that apply to the applicant, used for reporting.

Whether the applicant requires care support in their own daily life. Raw export column 66. Not secured: this is a support-need category of the same kind as rev_conditionprofile, which trustees see by design (TAD section 3.1). The free-text description behind it IS secured.

The applicant's own brief description of the care support they need day to day. Raw export column 67. SECURED - special-category free text under UK GDPR Article 9, same treatment as rev_otherconditionraw and rev_narrativeraw.
The name of the person who will receive the support, where this is not the applicant.
The general categories of condition that apply to the support recipient, used for reporting.

The free-text description of a condition affecting the person the applicant supports that is not covered by the standard list. Raw export column 78. Special-category data about a THIRD PARTY who did not themselves apply, so it carries the same restriction as the applicant's own equivalent (FR-031, NFR-001).

The types of care and support the applicant personally provides to the support recipient. Raw export columns 81-90. Not secured: a support-need category of the same kind as rev_conditionprofile, trustee-visible by design (TAD section 3.1).

Free-text description of a type of care the applicant provides that is not covered by the standard list. Raw export column 92. SECURED: special-category free text describing a third party's care needs, same treatment as rev_otherconditionraw.
A brief worked example of the level of care required, in the applicant's own words. Raw export column 93. SECURED: describes the support recipient's care needs in enough detail to be identifying.

On average, how many hours a week the applicant spends providing this care, one of five bands as sent by the live form (confirmed 2026-08-17). Raw export column 94. Not secured: a circumstance fact the trustees need to judge need, same basis as rev_amountrequested. Bands 4 and 5 overlap on the live form itself - see OptionSets/rev_carehoursband.xml.
The name of the person helping the applicant with this application, where one was given.
The email address of the person helping the applicant with this application.
The telephone number of the person helping the applicant with this application.

The organisation the person helping with the application belongs to, where they gave one. Raw export column 44. NOT secured, following the classification in docs/Import/grant-application-data-model-v0.2.md, which marks helper name, email and phone as PII and does not so mark organisation or relationship: the helper's identifying details are the name and contact columns, and those ARE secured.
How the person helping with the application is related to the applicant, in their own words. Raw export column 45. Confirmed against the live form 2026-08-16 to be free text, not a choice.
The name of the person providing a reference for this application.
The email address of the person providing a reference for this application.
The telephone number of the person providing a reference for this application.
The name of the person to contact in an emergency during the break.
The telephone number of the person to contact in an emergency during the break.

The ADMIN-ASSIGNED group reference the process owner sets by hand after the fact, to link the applications that belong to one holiday (raw export column 7, 'Group'). This is NOT the applicant's own answer about a group trip - that is rev_isgrouptrip and rev_groupmembernames below. Keeping the two apart matters: the combined-amount check groups on this column, and an applicant saying 'yes, this is a group trip' does not by itself tell the charity which other applications it belongs with.

displayname.description: Is Part of a Group Trip

Description.description: Whether the applicant says this break is part of a group trip. Raw export column 134. No default value, so 'not answered' stays distinguishable from 'No'.

The names of the other people travelling as part of the same group, as the applicant gave them. Raw export column 135. SECURED: these are third-party identities captured with this application, the same class of data as rev_supportrecipientname and rev_emergencycontactname, and FR-051 requires an erasure request to be able to reach them.
The kind of break the applicant is asking for. Raw export column 114. The option list is a PLACEHOLDER and must be confirmed with the process owner - see OptionSets/rev_breaktype.xml.

The kind of break the applicant is asking for in their own words, collected only when rev_breaktype is 'Other'. Raw export column 115. The existence of this column in the export is the proof that rev_breaktype's list carries an 'Other' option.

Where the applicant wants to go, or the name of the activity. Raw export column 116. TRUSTEE-VISIBLE ON PURPOSE and therefore deliberately absent from REV_TrusteeRestricted - the board cannot judge a request without knowing what is being requested. It is a place, not a person, so it carries no identity. Distinct from rev_providerpreference, which names a care provider.
The date the applicant would prefer their break to start.
The date the applicant would prefer their break to end.
The care provider the applicant has asked for, recorded as free text until the provider list is built.
The grant amount the applicant has asked for.
What the applicant expects the accommodation or the activity itself to cost. Raw export column 119.
What the applicant expects to spend getting to and from the break. Raw export column 120.
Any other cost the applicant expects, such as care cover or equipment hire. Raw export column 121.
The total estimated cost of the break. CALCULATED as accommodation plus travel plus other cost - it cannot be typed or written by a flow, so the parts and the total can never disagree.
Whether the applicant is receiving funding for this break from anywhere else. Raw export column 124. No default value, so 'not answered' stays distinguishable from 'No'.
Who else is funding part of this break. Raw export column 125.
How much funding the applicant is getting from that other source. Raw export column 126.

Any other funder the applicant has applied to and is still waiting to hear from. Raw export column 127. Operationally distinct from rev_otherfundingsource: money already promised versus money that may or may not arrive.
Whether the applicant is asking for funding above the normal level because of exceptional circumstances. Raw export column 128.

The category of exceptional circumstance behind the request, one of four options confirmed against the live form 2026-08-17. Raw export column 129 (distinct from column 128, rev_exceptionalfundingrequested). Deliberately NOT secured - trustee-visible by the same rule as rev_conditionprofile, see this attribute's own comment (TAD section 3.3, ADR-023).

The exceptional circumstance in the applicant's own words, collected only when rev_exceptionalcircumstance is 'Other'. Raw export column 130. SECURED: free text describing why circumstances are exceptional is very likely to be health or bereavement information, even in 200 characters.
The applicant's own explanation of the exceptional circumstance. Raw export column 131. SECURED - special-category free text, same treatment as rev_narrativeraw.

The extra amount requested on top of rev_amountrequested because of the exceptional circumstance. Raw export column 132. Held separately rather than folded into rev_amountrequested so that the normal request and the exceptional uplift stay separately auditable.
Whether the applicant says they have received funding from Revitalise before. Raw export column 136. Self-reported - the authoritative check is the deferred FR-023 duplicate-grant check.

displayname.description: Previous Funding More Than 12 Months Ago

Description.description: Whether that previous funding was more than twelve months ago. Raw export column 137. Asked only when rev_receivedfundingbefore is true.
Whether the applicant accepted the grant terms and conditions. Raw export column 12.
When the applicant accepted the grant terms and conditions, kept as evidence.

Whether the applicant confirmed the age declaration on the form. Raw export column 31. This is the column the under-18 question turns on (form specification OPEN-14): Phase 1 records it and takes no automated action on it, because no source says whether a person under 18 may apply in their own right.
When the applicant gave the age confirmation, kept as evidence.

Whether the applicant gave the applicant declaration on the form. Raw export column 46. Note that the charity's lawful basis for processing is NOT consent (SDD section 7.2, UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(f) with Art. 9(2)(b)/(h) for the health data) - this column is a record that a declaration was made, not the basis for processing.
When the applicant gave the applicant declaration, kept as evidence.

The explanation given alongside the applicant consent declaration, in the applicant's or helper's own words. Raw export column 49. SECURED: an explanation of why a third party is acting for the applicant routinely names a health reason, same treatment as rev_caresupportdescription.
Whether the person helping the applicant gave the helper declaration. Raw export column 50. Collected only when a helper is involved, so an absent value is normal rather than incomplete.
When the helper gave the helper declaration, kept as evidence.

Whether the applicant asked for a paper form to be posted to them. Raw export column 148. LOW PRIORITY AND POSSIBLY MOOT: the redesigned digital-first form (Automation #1) may not offer a postal route at all, in which case nothing will ever set this column. Built for completeness against the export; flagged in the Dev Summary as a question for the process owner on whether a postal fallback is still offered.

displayname.description: How Did You Hear About Us

Description.description: How the applicant heard about Revitalise. Raw export columns 138-146. Not secured: a marketing/referral-source reporting dimension, not personal or special-category data.

displayname.description: Other - How Did You Hear About Us

Description.description: Free text given when 'Other' is selected for how the applicant heard about Revitalise. Raw export column 147. Not secured, same basis as rev_hearaboutus.

The applicant's narrative after identifying detail has been removed, written by REV | Narrative | Scrub Free-Text (TAD section 5.5, WBS 5.2 - DEFERRED, EX-003). Trustee-visible by design (FR-026) once released - see rev_redactionreleased. MaxLength matches rev_narrativeraw's, the column it is derived from. NOT secured: unlike rev_narrativeraw, this column's whole purpose is to be safe for a trustee to read; securing it would defeat that purpose. Its safety currently rests entirely on the fact that nothing has written to it yet.

The human-in-the-loop release gate (TAD section 5.5, FR-029, FR-030): rev_narrativeredacted is trustee-visible only when this is true. Written by REV | Narrative | Scrub Free-Text and the process owner's manual review step (WBS 5.2/5.3 - DEFERRED, EX-003), so this stays false on every row until that automation lands - the fail-closed default the TAD describes, not a gap. DefaultValue=0: a new application must never default to released.

Scopes trustee visibility to the current review round (TAD section 3.1, FR-038): set by the process owner to open an application to the portal for the round named in rev_reviewround. DefaultValue=0 - a new application is never visible to a trustee until deliberately opened, the other half of TAD section 5.5's fail-closed visibility gate alongside rev_redactionreleased.

Scopes trustee visibility to the current review round (TAD section 3.1, FR-038) - the same concept as rev_review.rev_round, on the other side of the relationship, and copied from it exactly (nvarchar, MaxLength 50, Format text, no value list). Free text: the TAD names the column but gives no format.

Trustee-visible by design once rev_redactionreleased is true. NOT secured: unlike rev_caresupportdescription, this column's whole purpose is to be safe for a trustee to read; securing it would defeat that purpose. Its safety currently rests entirely on the fact that nothing has written to it yet.

The redacted counterpart of rev_careprovidedexample, written by REV | Narrative | Scrub Free-Text once extended (TAD section 5.5, WBS 5.2 - DEFERRED, EX-003). Trustee-visible by design once rev_redactionreleased is true. NOT secured, same reasoning as rev_caresupportdescriptionredacted above.

The redacted counterpart of rev_othercareprovidedtype, written by REV | Narrative | Scrub Free-Text once extended (TAD section 5.5, WBS 5.2 - DEFERRED, EX-003). Trustee-visible by design once rev_redactionreleased is true. NOT secured, same reasoning as rev_caresupportdescriptionredacted above. rev_otherexceptionalcircumstance is deliberately NOT given a redacted counterpart here - it belongs to FR-059, not FR-035's care-support panel, and no requirement names its free text (TAD section 3.2.1).
